title: Incremental slab allocator + slice-loading — arch review notes
body:
Meeting: Incremental slab allocator + on-demand model slice loading — architecture review
Date: 2026-03-09 10:30–11:45 PT
Location: Zoom / serving-runtime channel
Attendees: Samira (owner), Liam, Ava, Noah, Priya, Yara (SRE), Ben (platform-engineering)

Summary:
- Reviewed RFC draft proposing a hybrid incremental slab allocator (ISA) plus slice-on-demand loader for large model weights to reduce peak GPU memory without regressing 95th-pct latency goals.
- Agreement on core idea: partition model parameters into aligned "slices" (variable-sized shards per layer), maintain per-GPU slab arenas to minimize fragmentation, and load slices lazily based on KV/activation access patterns with fast warm-path prefetch hints.
- Main open risks: cold-path latency for rare long-context requests, interplay with caching layers (KV prefix cache), and complexity in quantized operator compatibility.

Problem statement (motivation):
- Customers increasingly run models with very large stateless context + multi-turn chat. Peak working set often exceeds allocable contiguous GPU memory due to fragmentation and transient KV cache growth. Full-model residency wastes capacity for workloads dominated by short contexts and small active key-value footprints.
- Need a memory management approach that: reduces resident weights, mitigates fragmentation, keeps tail latency SLAs, and composes with existing KV prefix cache and batching logic.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Slab arenas per device: allocate slabs in power-of-two buckets (64KB up to 16MB) tuned for kernel and KV cache allocation shapes. Slabs are backed by cudaMalloc or driver-level reserved segments to keep address stability for kernels requiring pinned pointers.
2) Slices: model parameters are chunked into logical slices aligned to slab sizes. A slice may contain contiguous rows (e.g., embedding chunks) or whole attention-head groups depending on layer type. Slices are described by metadata in an on-device slice table (compact bitset + LRU tag).
3) On-demand loader: missing slices are loaded from host or local NVMe via a fast loader thread that tries to satisfy synchronous warm-paths for expected upcoming tokens. For strict low-latency requests, loader implements a prioritized synchronous load with micro-batching of slice fetches.
4) Profiler-driven prefetch: runtime collects hot-slice usage histograms per model+route; model manifest can include prefetch hints per route (e.g., codegen for chat templates).
5) Eviction policy: hybrid LRU for slices + priority preservation for KV cache and pinned operator buffers. Eviction throttling when device memory pressure nears SLO thresholds.
6) Fallback: if synchronous load would violate latency SLO, automatically route to a compatible full-residency lower-tier model variant (existing routing policy).

Design decisions and rationale:
- Slab vs buddy allocator: slabs reduce cross-kernel fragmentation and are easier to tune for typical layer shapes (matrix rows, embeddings). Buddy would give less internal waste but higher coalescing complexity. Chose slabs to prioritize predictability and fast constant-time allocation.
- Slice granularity: chosen heuristic is "max contiguous rows fitting in 4MB" for dense layers, 512KB for embeddings. Rationale: trade-off between fetch overhead and eviction granularity. We will validate empirically.
- Sync vs async loads: default behavior is async background streaming, but critical-path loads (hot-path first access) will do sync fetch if predicted latency cost is < 4ms. Threshold configurable per customer tier.
- Metadata location: keep slice table on device for O(1) hit checks; updates go through a compact atomic ring to avoid host round-trips. Simpler to implement than host-only metadata and reduces ioctl/host->device hops.

Alternatives considered (brief):
- Whole-model streaming (single-process swap akin to CPU swap): simpler but leads to large tail latencies and poor multi-tenant pressure isolation.
- Pure quantization + compression: complementary but doesn't address fragmentation and transient KV spikes.
- Virtual memory backed by driver (cudaMemcpyAsync + unified addressing blackbox): depends heavily on vendor behavior and offers less predictable latency for tuning SLAs.

Compatibility concerns:
- Quantized kernels: some custom int8 kernels expect contiguous weight pointers; we will need lightweight indirection support (pointer table) or buffer relocation at kernel launch. Action: Noah to prototype pointer-table shim for int8 matmul.
- Operator fusion and JIT: fused kernels that assume contiguous blocks must be handled by either materializing contiguous slices pre-launch or providing a migratory copy path.
- NVLink and multi-GPU sharding: slab arenas must be aware of inter-GPU transfers; prefer local slabs with explicit cross-GPU slice replication only for pinned hot-slices.

Performance goals (target metrics):
- Reduce average resident weight by 35–60% depending on workload (target 45% for chat-short contexts).
- 95th-pct latency regression <= +3ms vs baseline for hosted tier; for dedicated tiers, regression threshold configurable by SLA.
- End-to-end cold-load amortized < 12ms for typical slice set (goal 8–10ms after prefetch tuning).

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How to safely measure and surface slice load latencies per request to SLO instrumentation without adding noise? (Priya + Yara to propose telemetry hooks)
- Interaction with existing KV prefix cache eviction when both contend for slab space. Needs an arbitration policy rather than pure LRU.
- Storage backend: host RAM vs NVMe; cost/benefit trade-offs across dedicated/private deployments.
- Security and provenance: slice metadata must be signed in Private deployments to avoid tampering during on-device loads.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Noah: prototype pointer-table shim for int8 matmul to validate compatibility with quantized kernels. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Ava: implement micro-bench harness to measure cold-path slice load latency across NVMe and host memcpy flows. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Liam: update routing policy playbook to include automatic fallback triggers for ISA cold-path violations. Draft due: 2026-03-18.
- Priya + Yara: propose telemetry plan (span events, histograms, percentiles) and minimal tagging to integrate with Console. Due: 2026-03-15.
- Samira: update RFC with stated slab sizes, slice heuristics, and a compatibility appendix for quantized kernels. Version bump and post to Confluence. Due: 2026-03-12.

Notes-to-self and implementation hints (informal):
- Keep on-device slice table tiny: bitset for residency + 8-bit hotness tag + 24-bit LRU timestamp maybe sufficient to avoid atomic-heavy updates.
- Consider a two-pass loader: first pass issues batched mapped reads for slice headers to estimate size/hotness, second pass fetches full slice only when needed.
- For small models, bypass ISA to avoid overhead; detect via model-profile threshold.
- Test fuzzing: create adversarial pattern that spikes random long-context accesses to exercise eviction + load thrash.

Meeting decisions (explicit):
- Proceed with prototype phase (POC) focused on correct semantics and measurable microbenchmarks. No immediate rollout to hosted tier until telemetry and thresholds validated.
- Prioritize compatibility with quantized kernels in the POC; if incompatible, evaluate pointer indirection vs copy-on-launch cost trade-offs.

Next meeting: 2026-03-23 10:30 PT — POC demo + microbench results

References and related reading: see linked_artifacts above. Also: internal note "runtime/alloc-profiles/2026-q1" for baseline allocation shapes.

End of notes.
